statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is in the low band, below the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail is 17% with NQ holding a roughly 55-point two-sided band since the futures reopen, volatility decaying and cross-assets stabilising after the Federal Reserve's 16 September increase. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers Friday's release stack and the quarterly expiration cash open at 13:00-14:30 UTC, the only projected block-band hour. The Bank of Japan statement window at 02:30-03:30 UTC, the 06:30 UTC press conference and the 20:00 UTC expiration settlement are treated as conditional checkpoints rather than current blocks. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a narrow overnight band into a near-fully-priced Bank of Japan hike and September quarterly expiration
body: NQ is trading near 29,696.00, down about 47 points or 0.16%, inside a 29,674.00-29,728.50 band as of 00:17 UTC, roughly two and a quarter hours after CME equity futures reopened. The band has not widened since 23:17 UTC, no directional impulse has formed, and retracements remain freely available, which is the condition a mean-reversion process depends on. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,446.98, up 501.92 points or 1.73%, inside a 29,305.90-29,494.95 range, recovering most of the decline that followed the Federal Reserve's 25 basis point increase to a 3.75%-4.00% target range on 16 September, approved by a 12-0 vote. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.7% and the S&P 500 1.1% on the day. Cross-asset evidence is constructive rather than stressed: the VIX fell 12.82% to 15.44, the 10-year Treasury yield eased about five basis points to roughly 4.94% after snapping an eight-day rising streak, and WTI crude slipped to about $100.88 with Brent near $103.72 as Saudi Arabia moved to restore roughly half of its damaged East-West pipeline within days and routed additional cargoes through ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz. The Nikkei 225 opened 0.85% higher at 64,679.59. Delayed latest-session context showed all eight tracked megacaps higher and a broad semiconductor advance led by ARM, Intel, AMD and Micron; that is daily-change data and is not evidence of live price path. Two conditional catalysts define the next 24 hours. The Bank of Japan concludes its two-day meeting today, with the statement expected in a 02:30-03:30 UTC window and Governor Ueda's press conference scheduled for 06:30 UTC. A Reuters poll found 97% of 68 economists expect a move and about 89% expect 25 basis points to 1.25%, the highest since 1993, so the asymmetric surprise is a hold or a change in the tightening-pace guidance rather than the hike itself; yen-carry transmission is the credible channel into index futures, with USD/JPY near 153 after falling from about 160. Today is also the September quarterly expiration, which concentrates mechanical flow into the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 20:00 UTC settlement. Neither catalyst is treated as observed structure at this time.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 23:00 UTC are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Tail ranged between 17% and 26%, peaking at 26% in the 13:00 UTC hour around the U.S. cash open and easing to 17% by the 23:00 UTC hour after futures reopened. Stress fell steadily from 70% to 41% as post-Fed repricing resolved in an orderly way and implied volatility decayed. The dominant mode was recorded as trend-up through most of the cash session, reflecting a persistent but measured upside recovery, and returned to normal once the evening band formed.
outlookSummary: The projected path holds 17% through the current thin U.S. evening hour, then steps into the watch band as Tokyo trades the second day of the Bank of Japan meeting. It peaks for the Asian session at 23% in the 03:00 UTC statement window, returns to 22% around the 06:30 UTC press conference and eases to a 19% floor through the European morning. Its only conditional block-band reading of 25% falls in the 13:00 UTC hour, which stacks August Industrial Production at 13:15 UTC, a Federal Reserve speaker at 13:30 UTC and the quarterly expiration cash open at 13:30 UTC; that hour anchors the danger window. A second conditional step to 23% covers the 19:00 UTC witching hour into the 20:00 UTC expiration settlement, after which equity index futures close for the weekend at 21:00 UTC and the path falls to a residual floor near 14%. Stress tracks the same shape between 31% and 52%. Every forecast hour beyond the current one describes conditional risk, not observed structure.
